_comment: Config for setup-tc-board.py. Copy this, edit the Module options to your
own product areas, and leave the rest alone unless you have a reason.
Status, Priority, Automation Status and Role are deliberately NOT
domain-specific -- they are what the maintenance pipeline and the review
digest read. Module is the only field you are expected to rewrite.
Colours are cosmetic except where noted below.
title: Test Case Management

fields.name: Status
_why: The keystone. The two '(Under Review)' states let automation PROPOSE a
change without asserting it is correct: the agent may set those, and
only a person promotes to Approved or Deprecated.
Remove them and there is no safe way to run the pipeline unattended,
and nothing for the review digest to report.

options.name: Updated (Under Review)
options.description: Automation changed it; awaiting a human

options.name: Deprecated (Under Review)
options.description: Automation proposes retiring it; awaiting a human

options.name: Bug
options.description: The case documents a defect, not intended behaviour

fields.name: Module
_why: The ONE field to rewrite for your product.
Name options '<Category> — <Module>'. The prefix is load-bearing: the
duplicate check scans a whole category by it, and the digest groups by
it. Pick a convention and hold it.

fields.name: Priority
fields._why: Drives which cases are automated first and which run in a smoke pass.

fields.name: Automation Status
_why: The seam between this catalogue and your automated suite.
'Needs Review' is set automatically when an AUTOMATED case changes,
meaning its spec probably no longer matches. Those items are the
backlog where QE and automation actually meet.

options.name: Needs Review
options.description: Case changed; the automated test may now be wrong

fields.name: Role
fields._why: Who performs the case. Rewrite to your product's actor types.

fields.name: Review Notes
fields._why: Reviewer-owned. The maintenance agent is told never to read or write it.
